title: Addition of tangent maps on the dual-number diagonal
statement: For schemes and morphisms $S,D,X,f,g$ and the three reduction equalities as in [lem-ag-dual-numbers-diagonal-coefficients], the morphism $g^*\Omega^1_{X/S}\to\mathcal O_S$ induced by the diagonal restriction of $f$ is the sum of those induced by its two axis restrictions. Each induced morphism is transported along its reduction equality before addition.

source.place: Lemma 33.16.2 proof, square-zero pushout addition; sectionwise arbitrary-base form and group unit-law application

proof.text: Use the reduction equality to transport each infDerivation to the pushforward along g. Equality induction shows that the transported omegaHom is homOfDerivation of the transported derivation.
Apply the sectionwise coefficient identity to obtain that the diagonal derivation is the sum of the two axis derivations.

The universal derivation detects equality of module maps. Evaluate the postcomposition of desc(D1)+desc(D2) on a section, using the factorization equations for D1,D2,D3, to prove desc(D3)=desc(D1)+desc(D2). The sheafification adjunction preserves sums, since its right functor is additive; then apply additive pullback-pushforward adjunction. This proves the desired equality of module morphisms.

proof_origin.place: Square-zero addition calculation, applied sectionwise over arbitrary base schemes; group-unit-law and universal-differential glue written by G3
